name: BottomNav
label: Bottom nav
description: Mobile tab bar for three to five destinations, in the Rift style or as iOS Liquid Glass or Material 3 Expressive.

props.name: items
props.description: Destinations, three to five of them

props.name: activeKey
props.description: Key of the destination for the current page

props.name: onValueChange
props.description: Called with a destination's key when it is pressed

props.name: platform
props.description:
Which platform's tab bar to draw. `default` is the Rift bar; `ios` is the
iOS 26 Liquid Glass capsule floating over content with a sliding lens
behind the selection; `android` is the Material 3 Expressive navigation
bar with a pill indicator behind the selected icon.

props.name: search
props.description:
A destination set apart from the rest, search unless its `icon` says
otherwise. On iOS it is its own glass circle beside the bar; elsewhere it
joins the bar as the last destination.

props.name: minimized
props.description:
iOS only: shrinks the bar to the selected destination alone, the way the
system bar minimises while the page scrolls down. Ignored on other platforms.

props.name: fixed
props.description: Pins the bar to the bottom of the viewport, above the home-indicator safe area

props.name: aria-label
props.description:
Accessible name of the navigation landmark. Defaults to "Tabs", distinct
from Nav's "Main", so a screen carrying both announces two different navs

props.name: badgeLabel
props.description:
Visually hidden text read after a destination's label when it carries a
badge, given the item's `badge`. Defaults to ", new" for a dot (`true`)
and ", 3 new" for a count; the leading comma and space are part of the text.
props.defaultExpression:
(badge: number | string | true) =>
  badge === true ? ', new' : `, ${badge} new`

props.name: linkComponent
props.description:
The component its links render with, such as Next.js's `Link`, so they
navigate through the app's router. Wins over a LinkProvider's; a plain
`<a>` when neither is set.

LinkComponent.description: A component that renders a link in place of a plain `<a>`, such as a router's.

LinkComponentProps.description:
The props a link component receives: every anchor attribute, the ref, and
an `href` that is always a string. Next.js's `Link` takes these as they
are; a router whose link takes `to` instead needs a one-line adapter:
`({ href, ...props }) => <RouterLink to={href} {...props} />`.
